2	
3	Build a single-page browser app with the provided framework, served by vite. It must render one full-viewport canvas with id #app. The scene is a sky full of floating rock islands at sunset. Show at least 6 islands of different sizes, each a chunky rock underside tapering downward (cone or inverted-lump shapes) topped with a grassy surface and a few simple trees or crystals. Islands bob gently up and down at different speeds and phases. A warm orange to pink gradient sky fills the background with a large low sun, and 8 or more soft cloud banks drift slowly past at different depths. A thin waterfall or particle stream falls from the largest island. Distance haze makes far islands paler and bluer. The camera slowly drifts in a wide arc, looping every 40 to 60 seconds, with no user input. Do not rely on external downloads; build everything procedurally. Keep it above 30 fps on a mid-range laptop.

I wrote `src/main.ts`, a procedural floating-islands sunset scene. It passes `typecheck`, but I couldn't run `vite build` or render a frame, so the look and frame rate are unchecked.

- **Islands:** 11 islands of different sizes. Each has a ragged inverted-cone rock underside and a domed grass top, both built with `geometry.define`. Trees are instanced cones on cylinder trunks, and crystals are instanced emissive shards. Each island bobs with its own speed, phase and amplitude, plus a slight sway.
- **Sky and sun:** `sky.gradient` blends orange at the horizon into pink and purple overhead. There's a large low emissive sun sphere near the horizon, with two directional lights and bloom.
- **Clouds:** 15 cloud banks at depths from about -40 to -320. Each is one instanced mesh of squashed spheres that drifts at its own speed and wraps around. One fixed bank sits at the base of the waterfall as mist.
- **Waterfall:** a tapered four-box stream hangs from the largest island, with 44 animated droplets that shrink as they fall.
- **Haze:** distant islands and clouds are tinted pale blue-lavender or pink by their distance from the camera. I did this by colour instead of using fog.
- **Camera:** it moves on an ellipse with a 48-second loop through `app.camera.setPose`, and takes no user input.
- **Contract:** the app draws into `#app`, runs on `requestAnimationFrame`, and sets `window.__EVAL_READY__` after the first frame.

The sky gradient, the emissive sun, the water opacity and the bloom strength are my guesses at how the engine renders them. If the first capture looks off, those are the values to tune.
